# `silk/core/static_map`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Maps from text keys to values that exist only during static evaluation.

## When to use
Use [`StaticMap`](#StaticMap) to look values up by name while a `static fn` runs, such as the options a
command line parser derives from its declared fields. Use `silk.collections.hash_map.HashMap`
for a map at runtime.

## Details
A static map has no runtime value. It keeps its keys in insertion order, and each operation
returns a new map without changing its input. A lookup compares keys one by one, which suits the
few dozen entries a static description holds.

## Examples
### Count the options of each kind
```silk
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.core.static_map { StaticMap }

static fn shorts() -> StaticMap<u8> {
  let mut result = StaticMap<u8>.empty()
  result = StaticMap<u8>.insert(move result, "verbose", 118)
  result = StaticMap<u8>.insert(move result, "quiet", 113)
  return move result
}

static fn shortOf(name: string<'static>) -> u8 {
  let map = shorts()
  return match StaticMap<u8>.get(&map, name) {
    Option<u8>.Some {value} => value
    Option<u8>.None => 0
  }
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  static if shortOf("quiet") != 113 { compileError("quiet has no short form") }
  return 0
}
```

## `StaticMap`

```silk
pub struct StaticMap<Value>
```

An immutable map from `string<'static>` keys to `Value` values, built during static evaluation.

### Details

Every operation is `static`. Inserting a key that is already present replaces its value and
keeps its position.

### Method `insert`

```silk
pub static fn insert(self: Self, key: string<'static>, value: Value) -> Self
```

Returns a map with the entries of `self` and `key` mapped to `value`.

#### Details

A key already present keeps its position and takes the new value. To build a map in a loop,
assign the result back to the same binding, as in `map = StaticMap<u8>.insert(move map, "a", 1)`.
